description: Two logic gates, each taking two inputs and giving both a result and its inverse, with the gate chosen by a button and shown on a column of lamps

params.text: Steps that gate through AND, OR and XOR and back round to AND; the button's artwork is the same in all three positions, so the lit lamp beside it is the only indication of which one is chosen

inputs.text: The first input to that gate; with nothing patched here the gate is switched off, both of its outputs are held at 0V and none of its lamps lights
The second input to that gate; with nothing patched here the gate becomes a NOT of the other input whatever the button says, and the NOT/THRU lamp comes on

outputs.text: 10V while the gate is true and 0V while it is false, giving AND, OR, XOR or, with the B input empty, NOT of the A input
0V while the gate is true and 10V while it is false, giving NAND, NOR, XNOR or, with the B input empty, a buffered copy of the A input

notes: an input counts as high above 5.1V and low below 4.9V, and between those two the gate holds whatever it decided last
the lamp between a gate's two output jacks shows green while that gate is true and red while it is false, and is dark while the gate is switched off
the lamps are marked AND/NAND, OR/NOR, XOR/XNOR and NOT/THRU: the first word of each pair is what the plain output gives, the second what the barred output gives
the button has no effect while the B input of its gate is empty; the gate is a NOT in that case and stays one
one channel per jack; a polyphonic cable is reduced to its first channel

inputs.0:
high above 5.1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
